description: The roundplate part falls off the linear track boundary after reaching the ramp/pot-trap area instead of continuing forward on the feeder, consistent with post-track rejection where the part is pushed off the right side of the ramp.

The video sequence represents a normal process where the lego roundplate moves along the linear feeder and successfully traverses the ramp structure. There is no visual indication of the part being pushed off-track (pre-trap or post-track rejection), nor is there evidence of it falling off the track sideways or vertically in an anomalous manner. The object maintains its position on the track surface throughout the sequence as expected for normal behavior.

The video sequence shows the object climbing the ramp (images 1-5), but upon descent it does not appear to make a clean transition to the right-side linear feeder as per normal behavior. Instead, images 6 through 10 show the object seemingly landing on a separate, vertically separated surface or getting ejected from the track boundary, failing to continue forward movement smoothly on the designated feeder path.

The input video sequence shows a lego roundplate moving along a linear vibration feeder and successfully crossing the ramp/trap structure. The part remains on the track boundaries throughout the movement, climbing the ramp unhindered and falling onto the right side as expected for normal behavior. There are no visual indications of the part being pushed off the track vertically or sideways (post-track or pre-trap rejection).

The input video sequence displays a linear track with ramp setup, but the majority of frames do not contain the expected lego roundplate object moving through the system. The normal process behavior shows an object traversing the ramp and feeder, yet these frames mostly show empty track space with only one frame containing a small circular object. This pattern indicates missing part behavior where the primary moving element is absent from most frames or motion is not captured properly, deviating significantly from the described normal operation of unhindered movement across the entire track mechanism.

The input video sequence displays the lego roundplate part on the linear feeder in a stable, horizontal configuration. The object remains aligned and flat on the track throughout the sequence, consistent with the RAG retrieved normal data images and the sub-sampled normal process. There is no visual evidence of the part being pushed off the track vertically (pre-trap or post-trap rejection), falling off the ledge without climbing, or oriented in a manner suggesting it will fall off the track. The behavior observed matches the expected normal process where the object moves unhindered towards the ramp."

The video sequence shows a linear vibration feeding process with a Lego roundplate moving from left to right. In frames 1-9, the part successfully approaches and crosses the ramp trap, moving unhindered onto the second track section in line with normal behavior. However, in frame 10, an anomalous small dot or detached visual element appears on the track surface where it should be continuing its motion smoothly. This change indicates that the part has been pushed off or stopped abnormally due to interactions with the ramp structure, fitting the criteria for post-track rejection (pushed off vertically after falling down the ramp).

The roundplate part was pushed off the linear feeder vertical to the part movement direction (sideways/downwards) after climbing over the ramp. This behavior is consistent with post-track rejection, where the object fails to stay on the track boundary and instead falls or is ejected from the right side of the ramp, unlike the normal process where it would continue moving forwards unhindered on the feeder.

Frames 1-9 of the video sequence show the roundplate moving normally from left to right across the ramp and along the linear feeder, consistent with reference normal data. However, image 10 clearly shows the roundplate having fallen off or been pushed from the right side of the track, appearing vertically separated from the feeder surface, which constitutes a post-track rejection anomaly not observed in the provided RAG or sub-sampled normal process clips.

The video sequence shows the roundplate moving linearly from left to right along the feeder, traversing the ramp structure in a manner consistent with normal operation. There is no visual evidence of vertical displacement or rejection (such as being pushed off the track before or after the ramp). The part remains within the boundaries of the feeder throughout the analyzed frames.

The part moves towards the ramp, climbs the ramp unhindered, and is positioned at the ledge to fall off. This matches the normal process behavior where the object falls onto the feeder after passing the trap. No anomalous behaviors such as pre-trap or post-track rejection were detected.

The video sequence shows a lego roundplate part moving linearly from left to right on the feeder track. It approaches the ramp trap, climbs it without obstruction (unhindered), and falls off the right side edge onto the lower section of the feeder. This progression aligns perfectly with the normal process described: 'move towards the ramp', 'Climb the ramp unhindered', and 'Fall off the ledge onto the right side'. There is no evidence of rejection, such as being pushed off sideways or falling before entering the trap. The sequence represents a successful execution of the linear vibration feeding simulation.

The part is oriented in a manner inconsistent with normal process flow, appearing to be pushed or stuck sideways near the ramp (trap) structure. Instead of smoothly climbing and falling forward to the right, the orientation suggests an anomalous interaction with the trap mechanism or a pre-trap misalignment that prevents normal progression. This falls under trap rejection as there is clear visual evidence that the part is not proceeding parallel to the track direction but is instead angled, likely being pushed off by the ramp geometry.

The lego roundplate approaches the ramp but fails to climb it unhindered. Instead of falling off the ledge to the right side as expected, the part is pushed off the track vertically (sideways), with a significant portion of the assembly dislodged from the feeder at the top edge of the ramp. This behavior deviates significantly from the normal process where the part should traverse the ramp cleanly and continue moving forward on the linear feeder.

The video sequence shows the roundplate approaching and climbing the ramp. However, compared to normal behavior where a single part passes unhindered and lands centered in the exit feeder, the input images (especially 7 and 8) show multiple circular objects or objects displaced significantly off the track boundary on the right side of the ramp. This indicates a rejection event post-trap rather than normal passage.

A detached piece is visible floating below the linear track boundary in the final frame of the sequence, indicating the part was pushed off vertically after falling the ramp, consistent with post-track rejection.

The video sequence shows the linear feeding process with a lego roundplate. While the part initially moves towards and passes over the ramp (the raised section of the track) without issues, in the final frames (specifically images 9-10), there is a clear visual indication of post-track rejection. The small circular dot (the roundplate) appears separated and vertically oriented from the main linear feeder structure near the end of the track. This contrasts with the normal behavior seen in reference data, where the part would fall smoothly onto the adjacent right-side feeder line without appearing pushed or clearly detached/vertically positioned off the track boundary as suggested here.

The video sequence shows the lego roundplate positioned on the flat section of the linear track, approaching the ramp (part trap). This state corresponds to the initial step of the normal process ("move towards the ramp"). Compared to the RAG retrieved normal data, which includes frames where the part is in similar pre-trap positions, there are no indications of anomalous behavior. Specifically, the part is on the track and has not yet been pushed off the track boundary vertically (pre-trap or post-track rejection) or fell over the ramp while moving parallel (trap rejection). The lack of significant positional change across the frames might relate to vibration blurring as described in the normal process, but strictly by position and lack of rejection signs, this is considered normal.

The sequence depicts a Lego roundplate traversing the linear feeder. The object is seen climbing the ramp (normal process behavior) and reaching the right side of the track. There are no signs of being pushed off, rejected by the trap, or falling incorrectly; it follows the normal path of moving from left to right unhindered.

The video sequence depicts a lego roundplate moving along a linear feeder track and traversing a ramp. Analysis of the provided frames indicates that the part remains consistently positioned on top of the grey feeder surface. There is no visual evidence supporting the anomaly categories described, such as pre-trap rejection (the part being pushed off the track before the ramp) or post-track rejection (the part being pushed off the track after falling from the ramp). The geometry of the feeder remains intact with the part fully overlapping the boundary in all frames, consistent with normal process behavior.
